Phase marks progress through a cycle. The source phase difference φ is measured in radians (one turn is 2π). Editing φ pauses and keeps the current P and time t; all traces are immediately recalculated. Arrival phase also includes propagation: δ=φ−2π(r₂−r₁)/λ. Here d=r₂−r₁ is signed. The absolute path difference used for the earlier in-phase cases cannot replace it at general φ.

Same P=(0, 2.50), same time t≈0s: y₁≈0.29A, y₂≈0.29A, y₁+y₂≈0.59A. Instantaneous displacement is not cycle amplitude.

Traces are the previous two cycles of the CURRENT-parameter analytic prediction, not recorded measurements; edits redraw the whole prediction. Right-end dots show this instant. Cycle amplitude is the largest excursion, so a zero sum now does not imply zero amplitude.

Directed path difference d=0 (0λ); source phase φ=0π rad, arrival phase δ≈0π rad. Cycle amplitude B=2A|cos(δ/2)|≈2A.

Reinforcement: the two waves arrive at P in step, rising and falling together; the combined amplitude is twice a single wave's.

Model: linear sinusoidal waves of the same frequency, equal received amplitudes and fixed phase difference (coherence). A=1 is normalized displacement and T=4s is a teaching setting. Spreading, attenuation, reflection and dispersion are omitted. Rings illustrate crest positions, not a fluid solution. Still points use only floating-point-scale tolerance; near cancellation remains nonzero and tiny amplitudes are not rounded to an exact zero.
